subject: Cognitive Science
title: Bottlenecks
description: A micro-lesson that makes Bottlenecks usable.

hook.text: A factory can make 1000 widgets per hour. But painting takes 200 per hour. Your output? Just 200.

buildup.text: A bottleneck is the single constraint that limits the entire system's throughput. Fix it, and flow improves.

discovery.text: Goldratt's Theory of Constraints says optimizing anything other than the bottleneck is wasted effort.

twist.text: Fix one bottleneck and another appears. The constraint just moves. Systems always have exactly one.

climax.text: In knowledge work, the bottleneck is often decision-making: everything waits for one person to decide.

punchline.text: Find the bottleneck. That's where the leverage is.

quiz.question: What does the Theory of Constraints recommend?

details.summary: A bottleneck is the constraint that limits an entire system's throughput. No matter how much you optimize other parts, the bottleneck determines the maximum output. Identifying and relieving the binding constraint is the highest-leverage intervention in any system.
details.whyItMatters: Most improvement efforts fail because they optimize the wrong thing. Finding the bottleneck tells you exactly where effort will actually move the needle.
takeaways: The bottleneck determines the system's maximum throughput
Bottlenecks shift once the current one is relieved

faq.question: How do you identify the bottleneck in a system?
faq.answer: Look for where work piles up. The step with the longest queue or the highest utilization is usually the bottleneck. In manufacturing, it is the slowest machine. In knowledge work, it is wherever tasks wait longest for attention. Measuring cycle time at each step reveals the constraint.

faq.question: What happens after you fix a bottleneck?
faq.answer: A new bottleneck appears elsewhere in the system. This is Goldratt's Theory of Constraints: improvement is an ongoing process of finding and relieving successive constraints. The system can never be completely bottleneck-free because there is always a weakest link.
